key_insight: A proposed GKP-encoded quantum secure direct communication protocol could transmit secret messages over more than 1000 km using third-generation quantum repeaters.
engineering_relevance: Cost-based optimization links secure distance, secrecy capacity, and repeater resources to guide scalable quantum network deployment.
method: Encode quantum information in GKP qubits to correct small phase-space displacement errors.
Use third-generation quantum repeaters to counter distance-dependent photon loss.
Optimize repeater deployment by balancing communication performance and resource cost.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations indicate secure transmission beyond 1000 km at a 23 dB squeezing level; the abstract reports no experimental demonstration.
watch_item: Practical feasibility depends on achieving 23 dB GKP squeezing and implementing reliable repeater operations at scale.
paper_title: Long-distance quantum secure direct communication with Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits
